metric.why: Distributed AI training is unusually intolerant of network degradation; a lossy fabric shows up as wasted GPU-hours before it shows up as an outage.
metric.metric: Network latency, packet loss, and bandwidth
metric.definition: Continuous measurement of round-trip latency, loss rate, and utilization on the facility's internal fabric and external transit.

reading.body:
Distributed AI training degrades silently when network latency or packet loss rises, burning GPU-hours before any outage alarm triggers. This makes continuous measurement of round-trip latency, loss rate, and fabric utilization a binding operational constraint.

The cost structure of data centers means that wasted compute is worse than brief downtime. A training run that completes slowly across weeks accumulates phantom costs in power, cooling, and opportunity loss that never appear on an uptime report. Network fabric quality therefore determines whether infrastructure actually delivers the compute it nominally provides.

This metric covers the internal network between servers and the external transit to other facilities. It does not measure how often these networks actually degrade, whether degradation follows predictable patterns, or how much wasted GPU-hours a typical facility absorbs. Those facts would show whether network quality is already a scaling bottleneck or still an emerging one.
